title: Who Was Jesus?
welcome_lead: Meet Jesus of Nazareth — the central figure of the world's largest religion.
meta_desc: KS3 Religious Studies adventure on the life of Jesus and his key teachings.
final_note: You can now explain who Jesus was and why Christians follow him.

walkthroughs.body_html: Jesus was born around 4 BCE, traditionally in Bethlehem, and grew up in Nazareth. He began teaching around age 30 and gathered twelve disciples. He performed miracles, preached love of God and neighbour, and challenged religious leaders.

Jesus taught people to love God and love their neighbour as themselves. He told parables (story-lessons), forgave sinners, and welcomed outcasts. The Sermon on the Mount is one of his most famous teachings.

Around 30 CE, Jesus was arrested in Jerusalem, tried, and executed by crucifixion under Roman rule. Christians believe he rose from the dead three days later — the resurrection — and this is the heart of their faith.

mcqs.q: What does the teleological (design) argument claim?
options: Apparent purpose, order or complexity in the universe implies an intelligent designer — Paley's watchmaker analogy is the classic example.
The design argument proves God created the world in seven days.
Aquinas's Five Ways are five Christian sacraments.
The design argument proves evolution is false.
Pelagius and Augustine agreed humans are born innocent.
Aquinas's Five Ways are five Christian sacraments.

Five distinct arguments for God's existence: from motion, causation, contingency, gradation of being, and final causes/teleology — collectively forming Aquinas's natural theology, not a single argument.
Aquinas's Five Ways are five steps of one cosmological argument.

mcqs.q: What was the Augustine vs Pelagius dispute about original sin?
options: Augustine argued humans inherit a corrupted nature from Adam (original sin) and cannot achieve salvation without grace; Pelagius argued humans retain free will to choose good without divine intervention and that sin is imitated, not inherited.
Aquinas's Five Ways are five Christian sacraments.
Pelagius and Augustine agreed humans are born innocent.
Original sin means Christians believe babies are evil.
